items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: So when we talk about people like Milt Hinton, George Duvivier, you know, they were doing record sessions all the time. They were great professional musicians.

ctx.x: Well it seems like the business has changed pretty rapidly. Like you probably have an agent? You have a manager. In years past a guy like Milt Hinton probably would do his own booking. Are there advantages and/or disadvantages to the way things are now?

Yeah. The scene is totally changed. Even in the last twenty years. It’s become much more industry driven. By that I mean record companies, particularly major record companies, booking agents, presenters, and I’m thinking of like festival presenters, club owners, have had a big influence and I think to a degree too much influence on who, which musicians get exposed. Prior to the 1980s, the music always took care of that. It was the relationships that you forged and the music. So when we talk about people like Milt…
Who started that by the way? Anybody know?
